text: hey much better some things though you could do better for some critique here is again, take a zoom out for a moment and think about the thing as a whole. there is a whole hell of a lot going on here and when a number of the ui is purely mocked up as systems then are being built in around it there needs to be a better alignment between these sorts of things because so let me just harp on some of the like blairingly obvious things that may or may not have been entirely in your lane of work specifically but are directly dancing around it when there is clearly something to be done. so the first thing is look at the immediate disconnect on startup i read into [Image #4] im on floor 1 and also the ground level. also though why are there even two of these to begin with. the one that is ON the map actually does something while the one on the toolbar is the mockup, but does that make the mockup the one that is wrong, i dont think so and the reason i say that is exactly the reason you just had to turn around and move your buttons to a new place before we could even start to review anything is your paint button was directly under this ground button which means this place on the ui overall is a bad place because there is no awareness of what is even there to begin with
resolution: The two floor controls are ONE (0a6e87ff7, rode the viewport cut): the toolbar's Floor pill was mock state (FLOORS labels) while the working control floated in the viewport as the Ground chip — and they disagreed at boot (Floor 1 vs Ground). floorIndex is now the REAL active storey (0 = Ground) driving the new editor-owned viewport's level (camera lift + pick plane, placements land on the storey slab); the action bar renders the one control as ▼ Ground/Floor N ▲ with the loader's exact level vocabulary, the floating chip is gone with the old pane, boot shows Ground on both because there is only one state, and cycle-floor steps the same real value. The toolbar spot under which PAINT originally landed is no longer occupied by anything floating — the viewport is clean.
